findings.claim: The row's two fields characterize web:Isa.49.15 incompatibly, and the book-order next row contradicts the boundary_rationale's characterization of the same verse.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale argues the back seam from a verse that opens as a third-person rhetorical question, its “only second-person element being the closing suffix” in אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ (oshb:Isa.49.15, tier: byte), explicitly “not an address opening in the second person”; strongest_rejected_alternative in the same row then grounds the same seam on “the second-person divine address that follows.” The book-order next row (span Isa.49.15-Isa.49.21) argues web:Isa.49.15 as Yahweh's second-person answer opening an address that runs unbroken across its 7 verses. The seam itself is sound on tier-1 bytes standing in the span's own verse, וַתֹּ֥אמֶר צִיּ֖וֹן (oshb:Isa.49.14, tier: byte), plus the speaker change at web:Isa.49.15, so the boundary survives; the warrant text does not. Digits re-swept clean: the forget-root stands in 9 verses book-wide with exactly 2 in ch 49 (skeleton tier, verse counts), and the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.49.13 is present under that type, single-witness.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the strongest_rejected_alternative's ground from 'the second-person divine address that follows' to the speaker change the boundary_rationale actually argues (narrator's report of Zion's words giving way to the divine answer), OR drop the 'not an address opening in the second person' clause from the boundary_rationale so the two fields and the neighbor row describe web:Isa.49.15 alike. Field repair only; span unchanged.

findings.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative discharges no rival boundary at all - it weighs only the unit_type tag.
findings.grounds: The field reads entirely as a category rival ('Tagging this span salvation_oracle ... was considered and set aside because its bytes carry a summons-and-self-vindication interrogative form'), and no rival span, seam, merge or split is tested anywhere in the row. Every other row in this batch names a rival span. Both seams are themselves tier-1 sound in their own bytes - the messenger formula opening oshb:Isa.50.1 at the front, and the fronted divine title with a first-person recipient at אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה (oshb:Isa.50.4, tier: byte) at the back - and the row correctly disclaims the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.50.3 as 'tier-3 corroboration only, and ... not the driver for this back seam', so the defect is adversarial completeness, not the boundary.
findings.proposed_change: Supply a rival-boundary sentence in strongest_rejected_alternative: the live candidate is extending this span through web:Isa.50.4 against the fronted lordship title, or attaching web:Isa.50.1-Isa.50.3 back to web:Isa.49.24-Isa.49.26 across the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.49.26. Keep the unit_type reasoning in device_notes, where it already stands. Field repair only; span unchanged.

findings.claim: An interior paseq seg inside this span is undisclosed.
findings.grounds: The paseq inventory records a seg at oshb:Isa.50.1 (single-witness, count-only) - inside this row's own span Isa.50.1-Isa.50.3 - and neither the prose nor boundary_evidence_refs mentions paseq anywhere. The book-order next row discloses its own three interior paseq sites (oshb:Isa.50.4, oshb:Isa.50.10, oshb:Isa.50.11) as single-witness count-only, so the omission breaks the cluster's own disclosure symmetry rather than reflecting a settled practice. No other row in this batch has a span-relevant paseq site (the inventory records none in ch 51). Parashah/K-Q disclosure for this row is complete and correct.
findings.proposed_change: Add a count-only paseq disclosure for oshb:Isa.50.1 in the prose and an 'oshb:Isa.50.1 (paseq, single-witness)' entry in boundary_evidence_refs, without any intra-verse position claim (the inventory is count-only). Field repair only.

findings.claim: A byte-uniqueness claim ships with no named count object and is false under its book-wide reading for the series' third member.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative says the series' first and third members repeat one shape 'from accent_stripped tier down, though byte-unique at their own sites'. Re-swept with the object named: the first member's opener שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י (oshb:Isa.51.1, tier: byte) stands at 1 verse book-wide at byte tier, but the third member's opener שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.7, tier: byte) stands at 2 verses book-wide at byte tier - its byte partner is oshb:Isa.46.3, which the row covering that span discloses explicitly. The row's own device_notes elsewhere handles this correctly (the accent_stripped digit of 4 verses book-wide, two sites outside the series, re-swept and confirmed at oshb:Isa.46.3, oshb:Isa.46.12, oshb:Isa.51.1, oshb:Isa.51.7). Not load-bearing: both seams rest on the imperative onsets themselves.
findings.proposed_change: Name the count object and the reading: replace 'byte-unique at their own sites' with a statement that the two openers are byte-distinct from each other, the third member's form standing at 2 verses book-wide at byte tier (the partner outside the series, at oshb:Isa.46.3). Field repair only.

findings.claim: A sentence-splice artifact stands in the shipped boundary_rationale.
findings.grounds: The mark-disclosure sentence reads '... interior to this span, and This span's own close carries a further SAMEKH mark (single-witness), at oshb:Isa.51.3.' - a mid-sentence capitalized 'This' where a clause was joined. The mark claims themselves are correct against the inventory: PE at oshb:Isa.50.11 at the front seam, SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.2 interior, SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.3 at the close, all under the claimed types with PE and SAMEKH not conflated.
findings.proposed_change: Re-join the clause ('... interior to this span, and this span's own close carries ...'). Mechanical field repair only.

findings.claim: device_notes carries a positional row reference, which campaign register law bars in any field.
findings.grounds: The everlasting-formula disclosure reads '... the identical run, לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה (oshb:Isa.51.8, tier: byte), closes the span two past it ...' - naming a neighbouring unit by ordinal distance rather than by verse anchor. Register law bars positional row references in every field and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored; the verse anchor is present here, so the ordinal is redundant as well as barred. All of this row's digits re-swept clean: the everlasting formula לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה is byte-identical at exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.51.6, oshb:Isa.51.8); the garment simile is an exact byte pair at oshb:Isa.50.9 and oshb:Isa.51.6, stands at exactly 3 verses word-bound skeleton (adding oshb:Isa.51.8), and its bare consonantal substring does reach a fourth site, which the row leaves uncited so no offset-zone dual-cite obligation is triggered.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'closes the span two past it' with the verse anchor already supplied (e.g. 'closes the unit ending at oshb:Isa.51.8'). Mechanical field repair only.

findings.claim: A byte-identity claim equates two runs of different extent; collated, they are not identical.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale asserts that וְצִדְקָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה (oshb:Isa.51.8, tier: byte) 'is byte-identical to' לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה (oshb:Isa.51.6, tier: byte). Collated, the three-token run at oshb:Isa.51.8 and the two-token run at oshb:Isa.51.6 are not equal at byte tier; what is byte-identical across the two verses is the two-token formula alone, and its sweep digit of exactly 2 verses book-wide is correct at byte, accent_stripped and skeleton alike. The neighbouring row states the same relation correctly, over the two-token run on both sides.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the claim to the two-token run on the oshb:Isa.51.8 side so the asserted identity matches collate truth, keeping the 'attached to my righteousness' gloss that already distinguishes the two sites. Field repair only.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale carries a positional row reference, which campaign register law bars in any field.
findings.grounds: The same sentence reads '... closing the span two before it (oshb:Isa.51.6, tier: byte) ...', naming a neighbouring unit by ordinal distance; register law bars positional row references in every field and requires verse-anchored cross-row references, which the parenthetical already supplies. The row's other digits re-swept clean: the opener's byte partner is at oshb:Isa.46.3 as disclosed; the moth and the worm are absent from oshb:Isa.51.6 at every tier; and no run of two or more tokens is shared at byte tier with oshb:Isa.50.9.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'the span two before it' with the verse anchor already present. Mechanical field repair only.

findings.claim: The back seam's only warrant in this row's own prose is a tier-3 parashah mark; no tier-1 signal is named and the seam's forward verse is absent from the evidence refs.
findings.grounds: For the Isa.51.11|Isa.51.12 seam the boundary_rationale offers only 'This span winds down at oshb:Isa.51.11, under its own parashah SAMEKH mark, witnessed in a single source.' The row never names what opens at web:Isa.51.12, and neither web:Isa.51.12 nor oshb:Isa.51.12 appears in boundary_evidence_refs; strongest_rejected_alternative addresses only the interior Isa.51.10|Isa.51.11 question. Owner law makes the parashah layer in the Prophets tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver, so as shipped this load-bearing edge has no admissible driver. Every other row in this batch names the next unit's tier-1 onset for its back seam. The seam is nonetheless correct on bytes: web:Isa.51.12 opens a doubled first-person divine self-identification, אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.51.12, tier: byte), so this is a warrant defect, not a boundary defect. The row's front seam is unaffected - it carries its own tier-1 imperative onset - and all its digits re-swept clean (the doubled onset byte-unique to its verse and matching oshb:Isa.52.1 from accent_stripped down at 2 verses book-wide; the third imperative giving a skeleton-token count of 3 in that one verse; the reflexive-shaped onset at oshb:Isa.51.17 unique at every tier; the joy-and-gladness pair byte-identical at exactly 3 verses book-wide).
findings.proposed_change: Add the tier-1 back-seam driver to boundary_rationale - the fresh first-person divine self-identification opening web:Isa.51.12 - and add web:Isa.51.12 and oshb:Isa.51.12 to boundary_evidence_refs, keeping the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.11 as the disclosed tier-3 corroboration it already is. Field repair only; the span is correct as cut.

findings.claim: An internal instance of the row's own declared tier-1 driver class stands inside the span, unweighed and undisclosed, across two verses the row's prose never engages.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals declares oracle_frame.addressee_shift, and this cluster treats addressee shift as a tier-1 class in its own prose. Inside the span the addressee marking turns: web:Isa.51.12 addresses a plural and then a feminine singular - מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם and מִֽי אַ֤תְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ (oshb:Isa.51.12, tier: byte) - while from web:Isa.51.13 on the marking is masculine singular: עֹשֶׂ֗ךָ (oshb:Isa.51.13, tier: byte), אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ (oshb:Isa.51.15, tier: byte), and בְּפִ֔יךָ with כִּסִּיתִ֑יךָ (oshb:Isa.51.16, tier: byte). The row's prose quotes only web:Isa.51.12, web:Isa.51.15 and web:Isa.51.16 and never engages web:Isa.51.13-Isa.51.14 at all; strongest_rejected_alternative weighs only the merge back across the front seam, so this rival is never tested. I do not propose a split: the divine speaker is continuous across web:Isa.51.12-Isa.51.16 and no frame token opens web:Isa.51.13, and the cluster's own precedent holds an addressee shift attached where no frame token accompanies it. The defect is the silence, compounded by confidence 'medium' with frontier_flag_considered false on a span whose closing verse carries the addressee question the row leaves unstated. Both seams are themselves tier-1 sound and both mark claims (SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.11 and oshb:Isa.51.16) are correct under type.
findings.proposed_change: Disclose the internal masculine-singular turn from web:Isa.51.13 on and weigh it explicitly as the rival it is (a candidate seam at Isa.51.12|Isa.51.13), holding the span on the continuity of the divine speaker and the absence of any frame token; engage web:Isa.51.13-Isa.51.14 in the prose; and recalibrate to confidence medium_low with frontier_flag_considered true. Field repair only; span unchanged.

findings.claim: At the closing verse the English gloss covers one clause while the Hebrew splice covers the whole verse.
findings.grounds: The row writes that the span closes at web:Isa.51.16 and glosses it with the verse's final clause only, “tell Zion, ‘You are my people.’”, while splicing the entire pointed verse from וָאָשִׂ֤ים דְּבָרַי֙ through עַמִּי אָֽתָּה (oshb:Isa.51.16, tier: byte). Gloss extent does not equal splice extent. The quoted English is itself verbatim WEB and carries an in-field web: ref, so this is a parity defect, not a quotation defect; the row's other verse-gloss slot, at web:Isa.51.12, has correct parity.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the gloss to the full WEB rendering of web:Isa.51.16 so it matches the spliced extent (or narrow the splice to the final clause and keep the short gloss). Field repair only.

findings.claim: An exclusivity claim ships without a digit or a named count object.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative calls the messenger frame at oshb:Isa.51.22 'ch 51's only messenger-formula site' with no digit and no swept object named (word-bound versus substring, and which chapter space). Re-swept: the formula כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר (oshb:Isa.51.22, tier: byte) stands at 48 verses book-wide by consonantal skeleton and at exactly 1 verse in ch 51, so the claim is TRUE; the row also correctly names the frame owner as divine and borne by Zion's own suffixed lordship title, which is the part of the koh-amar hazard that matters most. Everything else in this row re-verified clean: the cup runs at oshb:Isa.51.17 and oshb:Isa.51.22 match from accent_stripped tier down and not at byte; the goblet, cup and reeling nouns each stand at exactly 2 verses book-wide word-bound skeleton at those same two sites with the order inverted at the second; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.51.16 corroborates the front seam and the SAMEKH keyed to oshb:Isa.51.21 is correctly disclosed as falling one verse past the close and corroborating no seam of this row; the back seam rests on a tier-1 connective-plus-imperative in web:Isa.51.21's own bytes; and the binyan of the doubled onset is properly held as unsettled by the staged evidence.
findings.proposed_change: Add the sanctioned digit-bearing shorthand to the exclusivity claim, naming the object and the space (e.g. the divine messenger frame standing at exactly 1 verse in this chapter, 48 verses book-wide, word-bound skeleton). Field repair only.
